policies.policy_title: Increase NHS funding and staff pay
policies.stated: Commit to increasing NHS annual expenditure, rising to £28bn by 2030, and £20bn in capital spending over five years for hospital building and repair, including an immediate budget increase for fair wage settlements for staff.

source.quote: We estimate that to meet these commitments, the NHS in England would require additional annual expenditure of £8bn in the first full year of the next parliament, rising to a total of £28bn in 2030. We also estimate that additional capital spending of at least £20bn is needed in total over the next five years. We will prioritise supporting NHS workers, including by providing an immediate one-off budget increase to cover fair wage settlements.

policies.policy_title: Reduce NHS waiting lists and guarantee GP access
policies.stated: Commit to a steady reduction in hospital waiting lists by providing long-term funding commitments to trusts, and guarantee rapid access to a GP for all, with same-day access for urgent needs.

source.quote: We would bring down hospital waiting lists by giving Hospital Trusts clear, long-term, funding commitments, so that they can better plan to deliver better care for us all. Elected Greens will push for: • A steady reduction in waiting lists. • We would guarantee rapid access to a GP and same day access in case of urgent need.

policies.policy_title: Guarantee access to NHS dentistry
policies.stated: Introduce a new contract for NHS dentists and invest an additional £3bn a year by 2030 to ensure universal access to NHS dentistry, including free dental nursing for children and low-income individuals.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for a new contract for NHS dentists that ensures everybody who needs an NHS dentist has access to one. Additional investment in NHS dentistry, reaching £3bn a year by 2030, would transform the availability of appointments and end the scandal of dental treatment deserts. Elected Greens will campaign for funding to allow community hubs and primary care to provide a roll-out of free dental nursing for children and those on low incomes.

policies.policy_title: Increase public health funding and establish a commission on drug law reform
policies.stated: Restore public health budgets to 2015/16 levels with an immediate £1.5bn increase, properly funding services like smoking cessation, drug and alcohol treatment, and sexual health. Establish a National Commission to propose evidence-based reform of UK drug laws, moving towards a legally regulated market.

source.quote: Restoring public health budgets to 2015/16 levels with an immediate increase of £1.5bn. Smoking cessation, drug and alcohol treatment and sexual health services all need to be properly funded. A National Commission to agree an evidenced based approach to reform of the UK’s counterproductive drug laws. This will allow the UK to move towards a legally regulated market that stops criminal supply and profiteering, and that reduces harm including by preventing children accessing drugs.

policies.policy_title: Re-establish a fully public NHS and end privatisation
policies.stated: Defend the NHS against privatisation by abolishing wasteful competition, re-establishing public bodies and accountability, restricting commercial companies, and backing the NHS Reinstatement Bill.

source.quote: Protect our NHS from privatisation – keep our NHS public abolish wasteful competition within the NHS, reestablish public bodies and public accountability, and restrict the role of commercial companies. Green MPs will back the NHS Reinstatement Bill to public health.

policies.policy_title: Implement a National Cancer Control Plan
policies.stated: Introduce a National Cancer Control Plan to reduce cancer cases through public health investment, meet the 75% early diagnosis target by 2028 via primary care and screening, and deliver treatment through publicly funded research.

source.quote: We will commit to a National Cancer Control Plan to include: • Reducing cases through investment in public health measures, such as interventions on food, alcohol and tobacco. • Meet the existing NHS target of 75% of cases diagnosed at stage 1 or stage 2 by 2028 though investment in primary care and enhanced screening. • Using the unique information the NHS has, as a public health system that cares for us from cradle to the grave, to deliver treatment through publicly funded research.

policies.policy_title: Improve mental health care access and provision
policies.stated: Invest in primary care to improve access to mental health services, ensuring everyone can access evidence-based mental health therapies within 28 days, with tailored provision for specific communities. This includes trained counsellors in every primary and secondary school.

source.quote: Elected Greens will focus on enabling major improvements to mental health care to put it on a truly equal footing with physical health care. This will include ensuring that everyone who needs it can access evidence-based mental health therapies within 28 days. We will provide a trained and paid counsellor in every primary and secondary school, and every sixth-form college.

policies.policy_title: Introduce free personal social care and reform the care workforce
policies.stated: Introduce free personal care, funded by £20bn per year, along the lines of the Scottish model, to ensure dignity in old age and for disabled people. Establish a career structure for carers with national pay, terms, and conditions, and reform the working visa system to end exploitation of overseas care workers.

source.quote: Elected Greens will bring together local authorities, trade unions and private providers to establish a career structure for carers, ensuring there is a pathway to progression that includes training and qualifications. This would have national pay, terms and conditions for all care workers and a proper workforce plan. Elected Greens will also change the working visa system to end the exploitation of overseas workers in the care sector. To address the social care crisis elected Greens will push for: • Increased pay rates and a career structure for carers to rebuild the care workforce. • Investment of £20bn per year. • Free personal care to ensure dignity in old age and for disabled people.

policies.policy_title: Legalise assisted dying with safeguards
policies.stated: Support changing the law on assisted dying to allow people to choose to end their lives to avoid prolonging unnecessary suffering, provided it is their clear and settled will and proper safeguards are in place.

source.quote: Elected Greens will back changing the law on assisted dying. We support a humane and dignified approach to terminal illness, allowing people to choose to end their lives to avoid prolonging unnecessary suffering, if this is their clear and settled will. Proper safeguards would need to be put in place.

policies.policy_title: Restore and improve disability benefits and support
policies.stated: Restore disability benefits with an immediate 5% uplift, end the targeting of disabled people on benefits, oppose replacing PIP with vouchers, and make free transport mandatory for 16-18-year-old SEND pupils.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Restore the value of disability benefits with an immediate uplift of 5%. • End the unfair targeting of carers and disabled people on benefits. • Oppose plans to replace Personal Independence Payments (PIP) cash payments with ‘vouchers’, and in the long term reform intrusive eligibility tests like PIP. • Make it mandatory for councils to provide free transport for 16–18-year-old pupils with Special Educational Needs and Disability.

policies.policy_title: Increase funding for children's social care
policies.stated: Provide an additional £3bn to local authorities for high-quality children's social care, including consistent access to counsellors for children in foster care or adopted, and extend staying put arrangements for fostered young people until 21.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for an additional £3bn to be provided to local authorities to enable them to provide high-quality children’s social care. Elected Greens will also push for children in foster care or who have been adopted to have consistent access to a trained counsellor until it is no longer required. We would fund councils to extend staying put arrangements, so fostered young people can choose to stay with foster parents until they are 21.

policies.policy_title: Build new social homes and end Right to Buy
policies.stated: Provide 150,000 new social homes a year at social rents and end the 'right to buy' to ensure homes remain community assets.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push to: • Provide 150,000 new social homes a year and end the so-called ‘right to buy’, so that these homes can belong to communities for ever.

policies.policy_title: Empower local authorities to introduce rent controls and strengthen tenants' rights
policies.stated: Empower local authorities to introduce rent controls, end Section 21 no-fault evictions, introduce long-term leases, give tenants the right to demand energy efficiency improvements, and establish Private Residential Tenancy Boards for dispute resolution.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push to: • Empower local authorities to introduce rent controls. • End no-fault evictions. Rent controls: Elected Greens will give the power to local authorities to control rents if the local rental market is overheated. A new stable rental tenancy and the ending of no-fault evictions: Elected Greens will push to end Section 21 no-fault evictions and introduce long-term leases. Renters will also be given a new right to demand energy efficiency improvements. Private Residential Tenancy Boards: Elected Greens will introduce Private Residential Tenancy Boards.

policies.policy_title: Invest in home insulation, green heating, and climate adaptation for homes
policies.stated: Invest £29bn over five years to insulate homes to EPC B standard or above, £9bn for non-fossil fuel heating systems like heat pumps, and £7bn to adapt homes for hotter summers, prioritising a local authority-led retrofit programme.

source.quote: Elected Greens will invest: • £29bn over the next five years to insulate homes to EPC B standard or above, as part of a ten-year programme. £12bn of this will be to retrofit the social housing stock and £17bn as grants to retrofit privately owned homes to a similar standard. • £9bn over the next five years for heating systems (e.g. heat pumps) for homes and other buildings. • £7bn over the next five years to adapt homes to avoid over-heating in the hotter summers.

policies.policy_title: Reform the planning system for sustainable development and protect green spaces
policies.stated: Transform the planning system to reduce environmental impact, require small developments across areas, protect the Green Belt, ensure new homes meet Passivhaus or equivalent standards with solar panels and heat pumps, and ensure new developments are supported by infrastructure and discourage car dependency.

source.quote: We will transform the planning system to reduce the environmental impact of new construction and to require local authorities to spread small developments across their areas, where appropriate, rather than building huge new estates. Greens are also committed to protecting the Green Belt and ensuring everybody has easy access to a green space. Elected Greens will campaign to change building regulations so all new homes meet Passivhaus or equivalent standards and to require house builders to include solar panels and low carbon heating systems such as heat pumps for all new homes. New developments need to ensure that residents are not car dependent.

policies.policy_title: End new oil and gas licences and subsidies
policies.stated: Push the government to stop all new fossil fuel extraction projects in the UK, cancel recently issued licences like Rosebank, and end all subsidies to the oil and gas industries.

source.quote: Green MPs will push the next government to stop all new fossil fuel extraction projects in the United Kingdom and to cancel recently issued fossil fuel licences, such as for Rosebank. We will also end all subsidies to the oil and gas industries.

policies.policy_title: Accelerate investment in renewable energy to achieve zero-carbon electricity by 2030
policies.stated: Transition to a zero-carbon society more than a decade ahead of 2050, aiming for wind to provide around 70% of UK electricity by 2030, with targets of 80GW offshore, 53GW onshore, and 100GW solar by 2035. This includes new support, incentives, and ending the de-facto ban on onshore wind.

source.quote: The UK’s current climate targets do not reflect the urgency of the climate crisis or what is required by global justice. We would push the government to transition to a zero-carbon society as soon as possible, and more than a decade ahead of 2050. Green MPs will aim to introduce new support and incentives to directly accelerate wind energy development...This will pave the way for wind to provide around 70% of the UK’s electricity by 2030. Our targets are to achieve 80GW of offshore wind, 53 GW of onshore wind, and 100 GW of solar by 2035. We will end the de-facto ban on onshore wind.

policies.policy_title: Expand community and public ownership of energy infrastructure
policies.stated: Promote community ownership with a minimum threshold in all sustainable energy infrastructure, remove regulatory barriers, and invest in community energy via regional banks. Bring the Crown Estate into public ownership, devolving Welsh assets to the Welsh Government, and expand offshore wind and marine energy.

source.quote: We are committed to the energy sector being under local democratic control as far as is possible. We will push for: • A minimum threshold of community ownership in all sustainable energy infrastructure. • The removal of regulatory barriers to community energy. • Investment in community energy by regional investment banks. The Crown Estate will be brought into public ownership and should open more coastal waters for offshore wind and marine energy. Control over its assets within the jurisdiction of Wales should be devolved to the Welsh Government, as it is in Scotland.

policies.policy_title: Invest in a just transition to a zero-carbon economy
policies.stated: Invest £4bn per year in skills and training for workers in carbon-intensive industries to transition to green jobs, establish an Offshore Energy and Skills Passport, and ensure communities benefit from the shift to green energy.

source.quote: There needs to be a just transition, led by workers and unions, that sees communities reap the rewards of the shift to green energy. As part of this, we will push the next government to establish an Offshore Energy and Skills Passport so that workers can transition more easily between offshore energy industries. Elected Greens will push for: • Investment in skills and training (including retrofitting) reaching £4bn per year, allowing workers to be prepared for the transition and the new roles they can take on.

policies.policy_title: Improve and expand the electricity grid and energy storage
policies.stated: Significantly expand and improve the efficiency of the electricity grid, increase capacity for energy storage, and connect electricity supply more closely with Europe to ensure security of supply and enable energy export.

source.quote: Elected Greens will seek to significantly expand and improve the efficiency of the electricity grid, increasing its capacity so that it can distribute the increased electricity the UK will need as it transitions away from fossil fuels. We would connect our electricity supply more closely to that of our neighbours in Europe to provide a broader-based supply we can call on when needed and to allow us to export electricity when we have a surplus. We would rapidly expand the capacity for energy storage, so that there is security of electricity supply for short-term peaks in demand and periods of low supply from variable renewables.

policies.policy_title: Cease new nuclear power development and phase out existing stations
policies.stated: Cease development of new nuclear power stations due to high costs, slow development, and risks, and campaign to phase out existing nuclear power stations.

source.quote: We would cease development of new nuclear power stations, as nuclear energy is much more expensive and slower to develop than renewables. Green MPs will campaign to phase out existing nuclear power stations.

policies.policy_title: Invest in a Green Economic Transformation
policies.stated: Commit to an average of £40bn per year investment over the next parliament, including £7bn annually on climate adaptation, to deliver a green economic transformation with public and private sector involvement.

source.quote: Elected Greens would push for significant investment in a green economic transformation, alongside the private sector. This programme to include: • An average of £40bn per year over the course of the next parliament, including £7bn annually on climate adaptation.

policies.policy_title: Bring privatised utilities into public ownership
policies.stated: Immediately bring railways, water companies, and the Big 5 retail energy companies back into public ownership through public investment, to serve the public rather than shareholders.

source.quote: We commit to immediately bringing the railways, the water companies and the Big 5 retail energy companies back into public ownership. Public investment would buy equity in these public utilities, ensuring they are run to serve us all, rather than to increase the wealth of shareholders.

policies.policy_title: Require financial services to divest from fossil fuels
policies.stated: Require UK banking licence holders to present an investment strategy for divestment from fossil fuel assets by 2030, change the Bank of England's mandate to include funding sustainability, and require non-bank financial institutions to remove fossil fuel assets by 2030.

source.quote: Any company holding a UK banking licence will be required to present an investment strategy outlining a clear pathway to divestment of its current fossil fuel assets as soon as possible, and at least by 2030. The Bank of England’s mandate will be changed so that funding the sustainability transition becomes a central objective, alongside the maintenance of price stability. Non-bank financial institutions, such as UK pension funds, investment funds, mutual funds, brokers and insurance companies that sell policies in the UK, will need to remove fossil fuel assets from their investment portfolios, securities transactions and balance sheets by 2030.

policies.policy_title: Support SMEs and community enterprises for the green economy
policies.stated: Set up regional mutual banks with £10bn public money to invest in SMEs and community-owned enterprises for decarbonisation. Provide local authorities with £2bn per year in grants for businesses to decarbonise. Explore legal ways to transform companies into mutual organisations.

source.quote: Green MPs will back the setting up of regional mutual banks to drive investment in decarbonisation and local economic sustainability by supporting investment in SMEs and community-owned enterprises and cooperatives. These banks will be capitalised through a Cooperative Development Fund using some of the funds made available through the United Kingdom Infrastructure Bank (UKIB), along with an additional £10bn of public money. We will give local authorities £2bn per year to provide grants to help businesses decarbonise. We will explore legal ways for companies to be transformed into mutual organisations, especially at the point of succession from one owner to another.

policies.policy_title: Increase R&D investment for climate and environmental solutions
policies.stated: Increase investment into research and development by over £30bn across five years, focusing on energy storage, agroecological agriculture, circular economy, carbon-neutral construction, and carbon capture technology.

source.quote: Green MPs will seek to increase investment into research and development by over £30bn in the lifetime of the five-year parliament. Additional spending will be primarily focused on tackling the climate and environmental crisis through funding research into sectors including: energy storage; agroecological agriculture and soil health; re-use, repair, recycling and designing out waste; carbon neutral construction; carbon-neutral production and carbon capture technology.

policies.policy_title: Promote a circular economy and right to repair
policies.stated: Advocate for a circular economy by requiring manufacturers to offer ten-year warranties on white goods, introduce a comprehensive 'right to repair', eliminate built-in obsolescence, and mandate production of energy-efficient white goods, TVs, and lighting.

source.quote: Green MPs will advocate for a circular economy that reduces the waste of resources. We will require manufacturers to offer ten-year warranties on white goods, to encourage repair and reuse. We will introduce a comprehensive ‘right to repair’, so manufacturers keep goods operational years after purchase and to eliminate built-in obsolescence. We will require manufacturers to produce only the most energy efficient white goods, TVs, lighting and electric cookers.

policies.policy_title: Introduce a £15 minimum wage and 10:1 pay ratio cap
policies.stated: Introduce a minimum wage of £15 an hour for all ages, offsetting costs for small businesses by increasing the Employment Allowance to £10,000, and campaign for a maximum 10:1 pay ratio for all private and public-sector organisations.

source.quote: We will seek to introduce a minimum wage of £15 an hour for all, no matter your age, with the costs to small businesses offset by increasing the Employment Allowance to £10,000. Green MPs will campaign for a maximum 10:1 pay ratio for all private and public-sector organisations.

policies.policy_title: Strengthen workers' rights and trade union powers
policies.stated: Repeal current anti-union legislation, replace it with a Charter of Workers’ Rights, restore the right to strike, and provide full employment rights from day one for all workers, including gig economy workers and those on zero-hours contracts.

source.quote: Elected Greens would campaign to: • Repeal current anti-union legislation and replace this with a positive Charter of Workers’ Rights. • Deliver equal rights for all workers currently excluded from protections, including ‘gig economy’ workers and those on ‘zero hours’ contracts. We will legislate for workers to have full employment rights from day one of their employment. We will restore the right to strike, remove arbitrary ballot thresholds and outdated requirements for postal ballots for strike action, and overturn bans on secondary picketing and industrial action for political objectives.

policies.policy_title: Expand pay-gap protections and support flexible working
policies.stated: Push for pay-gap protections to be extended to all protected characteristics, including ethnicity, disability, and sexual orientation, ensuring equal pay for equal work and flexible working arrangements.

source.quote: Green MPs will push for pay-gap protections to be extended to all protected characteristics including ethnicity, disability and sexual orientation. We believe in equal pay for equal work and in the right to flexible working arrangements that will benefit women, carers and disabled people in particular.

policies.policy_title: Increase Universal Credit, benefits, and pensions
policies.stated: Increase Universal Credit and legacy benefits by £40 a week, end the five-week waiting period, abolish the two-child benefit cap, increase all disability benefits by 5%, uprate pensions with inflation and wage rises, and increase carer’s allowance by at least 10% a month. Scrap the bedroom tax.

source.quote: Elected Greens will campaign to: • Increase Universal Credit and legacy benefits by £40 a week. • End the unfair five-week wait for benefits which is pushing people into debt. • Abolish the two-child benefit cap and lift 250,000 children out of poverty. • Increase all disability benefits by 5%. • Ensure that pensions are always uprated in line with inflation and keep pace with wage rises across the economy. • Increase carer’s allowance by at least 10% a month. • Scrap the bedroom tax.

policies.policy_title: Introduce a wealth tax and reform capital gains and inheritance taxes
policies.stated: Introduce an annual wealth tax of 1% on assets above £10 million and 2% on assets above £1bn. Align Capital Gains Tax rates with income tax and NIC rates on employment income, reform inheritance tax, and remove the Upper Earnings Limit on National Insurance.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for a wealth tax. This will tax the wealth of individual taxpayers with assets above £10 million at 1% and assets above £1bn at 2% annually. Elected Greens will push too for the reform Capital Gains Tax (CGT) by aligning the rates paid by taxpayers on income and taxable gains. Elected Greens will also call for the reform of tax rates on investment income, by aligning them with the tax and NIC rates on employment income. We would remove the Upper Earnings Limit that restricts the amount of National Insurance paid by high earners. We would reform inheritance tax, ensuring that intergenerational transfers of wealth are taxed more fairly.

policies.policy_title: Introduce a progressive carbon tax
policies.stated: Introduce a carbon tax on all fossil fuels, whether produced or imported, proportional to greenhouse gas emissions. The tax would start at £120 per tonne and rise to £500 per tonne within ten years, designed to incentivise decarbonisation.

source.quote: Elected Greens will advocate for a carbon tax to incentivise businesses to decarbonise their supply chains and to help raise the money needed to shift to a zero-carbon economy. Elected Greens will propose levying a carbon tax at an initial rate of £120 per tonne, rising to a maximum of £500 per tonne of carbon emitted within ten years. This is deliberately designed to make it cheaper for the emitter to take steps to reduce emissions rather than pay the tax.

policies.policy_title: Reform property taxes towards a Land Value Tax
policies.stated: Work towards a long-term policy of Land Value Tax, re-evaluate Council Tax bands to reflect current values, and remove business rate relief on Enterprise Zones, Freeports, petrol stations, and most empty properties. Conduct a survey of all landholdings.

source.quote: Our long-term policy aim is a Land Value Tax so that those with the most valuable and largest land holdings would contribute the most. In the next parliament, elected Greens will take steps towards this by pushing for: • Re-evaluation of Council Tax bands to reflect big changes in value since 1990s. • Removal of business rate relief on Enterprise Zones, Freeports, petrol stations and most empty properties. • A survey of all landholdings to pave the way for fair taxation of land.

policies.policy_title: Increase business taxes and clamp down on tax avoidance
policies.stated: Increase the windfall tax on oil and gas production, close loopholes, introduce a windfall tax on banks with excessive profits, and make changes to VAT (reducing it on hospitality/arts, increasing on financial services/private education). Strengthen global tax agreements and HMRC resources to tackle tax dodging.

source.quote: Green MPs will support an increase in the rate of the windfall tax on oil and gas production and the closing of existing loopholes and tax-relief mechanisms. We would introduce a windfall tax on banks when excessive profits are being made. We would also propose a range of changes to VAT, reducing it on hard-pressed areas such as hospitality and the arts and increasing it on financial services and private education. It will be a priority to strengthen global tax agreements to stop corporate tax avoidance and evasion, and to ensure a level playing field between UK and transnational businesses. We will also ensure that HMRC has the resources it needs to reduce the gap between taxes due and taxes paid.

policies.policy_title: Introduce a Rights of Nature Act
policies.stated: Pass a new Rights of Nature Act to grant nature legal personhood, set soil quality standards, immediately phase out harmful pesticides like glyphosate, and introduce rigorous tests for all pesticides.

source.quote: Greens in parliament will make it a priority to pass a new Rights of Nature Act. For the first time, it would give Nature legal personhood, meaning that it could not be exploited for financial gain. The Act would also set standards for soil quality and phasing out the most harmful pesticides immediately (including glyphosate) and, as we move towards regenerative farming methods, introduce rigorous tests for all pesticides. Only pesticides that pass this test, and demonstrably don’t harm bees, butterflies and other wildlife, would be approved for use in UK and we would end the emergency authorisation of bee-killing pesticides.

policies.policy_title: Protect and restore 30% of land and seas for nature by 2030
policies.stated: Plan to give 30% of land and sea back to nature by 2030, ensuring permanent protection. Prioritise re-wetting peatland, increasing unharvested forest and woodland by over 50%, and create new protected spaces in urban settings. Make at least 30% of UK domestic waters fully protected Marine Protected Areas, banning destructive fishing practices.

source.quote: We would plan to give 30% of land and sea back to nature by 2030 ensuring that it is permanently protected. A priority would be the re-wetting of all peatland and increasing unharvested forest and woodland by over 50%. Elected Greens also commit to making at least 30% of UK domestic waters into fully protected marine protected areas by 2030. We will seek to ban all destructive fishing practices from Marine Protected Areas (MPAs) and other domestic waters.

policies.policy_title: Increase DEFRA budget and fund nature-based solutions
policies.stated: Increase DEFRA’s budget by £1.5bn to fund the Environment Agency and Natural England. Restore rivers, take a nature-based approach to flood prevention and storm overflows, and develop a soil health monitoring programme for England.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push to restore rivers and take a nature-based solutions approach to the prevention of flooding and storm overflows. We would increase DEFRA’s budget by £1.5bn, allowing an increase in funding for the Environment Agency and Natural England, to support the vital work they do to protect our environment. This would include developing a soil health monitoring programme for England, to match those in Scotland and Wales, to assess and understand changes in the health of soil over time.

policies.policy_title: Introduce a Right to Roam Act for England
policies.stated: Introduce a new Right to Roam Act for England, based on the Scottish model with sensible exceptions, to enable people to access green space close to where they live.

source.quote: Elected Greens will introduce a new Right to Roam Act for England, that would enable people to access green space close to where they live and be a first step to resetting our relationship with the natural world. This would be based on the model in Scotland and include sensible exceptions, such as fields where crops are growing.

policies.policy_title: Create a Commission on Animal Protection
policies.stated: Establish a new Commission on Animal Protection to oversee rules protecting animals from cruelty, uphold their rights as sentient beings, and apply the highest standards to companion, farm, and wild animals.

source.quote: Elected Greens will seek to create a new Commission on Animal Protection, responsible for overseeing all rules designed to protect animals from cruelty and upholding their rights as sentient beings not to be subjected to undue suffering. This Commission will ensure that the highest standards of animal protection are applied to companion animals, farm animals and wildlife - and that these standards underpin decision making by public bodies too.

policies.policy_title: Ban blood sports and strengthen animal cruelty laws
policies.stated: Ban all blood sports, including trail hunting and the commercial shooting of game birds, and strengthen and extend the 2004 Hunting Act. Introduce a licensing scheme for animal ownership and replace breed-specific legislation for dogs.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for: • A ban on all blood sports, including trail hunting and strengthening and extending the 2004 Hunting Act. Elected Greens would push for ending the exploitation of animals, including horses and greyhounds in racing. Green MPs will introduce a licensing scheme for the ownership of all kept animals and replace outdated breed-specific legislation for dogs with an updated dog control law.

policies.policy_title: End badger culling and invest in Bovine TB research
policies.stated: Campaign against badger culling, fund research into cattle vaccination for Bovine TB, and invest in better farm biosecurity and badger vaccination.

source.quote: Green MPs will campaign against badger culling. We will fund research into a sensitive test to enable cattle vaccination as part of a meaningful strategy to control the spread of the disease. We will also invest in better farm biosecurity and badger vaccination.

policies.policy_title: End factory farming and improve farm animal welfare
policies.stated: Push for an end to factory farming, enforce maximum stocking densities, prohibit the routine use of antibiotics in farm animals, and campaign for a complete ban on cages, close confinement, and deliberate mutilation of farm animals.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for an end to factory farming, enforce maximum stocking densities and prohibit the routine use of antibiotics in farm animals. Greens will campaign for a complete ban on cages and close confinement, and on the deliberate mutilation of farm animals.

policies.policy_title: Triple farmer support for nature-friendly farming
policies.stated: Almost triple support to farmers over the next 5-year parliament to support the transition to nature-friendly farming, conserve soil and the wider environment, and link farm payments to a reduction in pesticides and agro-chemicals.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Almost triple support to farmers over the next 5-year parliament to support the transition to nature-friendly farming. • Conserve and improve the health of the soil and the wider environment, which in turn would lead to cleaner rivers. • Link farm payments to a reduction in the use of pesticides and other agro-chemicals.

policies.policy_title: Increase domestic food production and promote healthy eating
policies.stated: Increase domestic food production, expand local horticulture, incentivize growing diverse plant foods, offer daily free school meals and breakfast clubs for children to Year 6, and include children in growing and preparing food as part of the core curriculum.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for: • Increasing domestic food production and expanding local horticulture. • Incentivising growing a much greater variety of plant food types to protect sourcing and enhanced nutrition. • All children to have a daily free school meal, made from nutritious ingredients and based on local and organic or sustainable produce and free breakfast clubs for children to Year 6. • Schools to involve children in growing, preparing and cooking food, as part of the core curriculum, so that they recognise and understand how to use basic fresh produce.

policies.policy_title: Rebalance power dynamics in the food supply chain
policies.stated: Rebalance the power dynamic between big food manufacturers and local alternatives, strengthen the powers of the Grocery Standards Adjudicator and Food Standards Agency, and regulate for fairness in negotiation and legally binding codes of practice.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for: • Rebalancing the power dynamic between big food manufactures and local alternatives such as local food networks, community-supported agriculture and other co-operatives. • Strengthening the powers of the Grocery Standards Adjudicator and the Food Standards Agency. • Reducing the vulnerability of the small-scale farming suppliers relative to the oligopolies in retail and food manufacture, by regulating for fairness in negotiation and new legally binding codes of practice.

policies.policy_title: Invest in early years education and childcare
policies.stated: Invest £1.4bn per year in Sure Start Centres and, in negotiation with the sector, extend the offer of childcare to 35 hours per week from nine months, focusing on play-based learning.

source.quote: Green MPs will advocate: • For £1.4bn per year to be invested by local authorities in Sure Start Centres. • In negotiation with the sector, to extend the outgoing government’s offer of childcare to 35 hours per week from nine months.

policies.policy_title: Increase school funding and teacher pay
policies.stated: Advocate for an £8bn investment in schools, including £2bn for a teacher pay uplift, and invest £2.5bn a year to tackle the RAAC concrete scandal and ensure school buildings are safe and well-maintained.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Advocate for an increase in school funding, with an £8bn investment in schools that would include £2bn for a pay uplift for teachers. • Ensure that every school building is safe for children by investing £2.5bn a year to tackle the RAAC concrete scandal and provide the funding needed for schools to be well-maintained and fit for purpose.

policies.policy_title: Reform school assessment and curriculum
policies.stated: Review assessment targets to treat arts and vocational subjects equally, support outdoor play and learning, include climate and biodiversity crisis education, ensure effective delivery of the Natural History GCSE, and end high-stakes formal testing.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Review assessment targets in schools so that arts and vocational subjects are treated equally within the curriculum, children are supported to play and learn outdoors, and every child can learn about the climate and biodiversity crisis to equip them for the challenges ahead. • Ensure effective delivery of the new Natural History GCSE. • Reduces the stress in our education system by ending high-stakes, formal testing at primary and secondary schools and by abolishing OFSTED.

policies.policy_title: Bring academies and free schools into local authority control and reform private school status
policies.stated: Move academies and free schools into local authority control, remove charitable status from private schools, and charge full VAT on private school fees, with an interim exemption for SEND children while public capacity is built.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Move academies and free schools into local authority control, removing charitable status from private schools and charging full VAT on fees. Private school places for children with special education needs will not be subject to VAT. This will be an interim measure while public-sector capacity is built.

policies.policy_title: Invest in special educational needs provision
policies.stated: Invest £5bn in special needs (SEND) provision within mainstream schools to ensure accessible buildings, specially trained teachers, and proper support for SEND students, including transport.

source.quote: Green MPs will push for £5bn to be invested in special needs (SEND) provision within mainstream schools. This means that all schools will have fully accessible buildings and specially trained teachers, and local councils will have the funds to properly support SEND students at school and in getting to school.

policies.policy_title: Restore maintenance grants and scrap tuition fees for higher education
policies.stated: Fully fund every higher education student by restoring maintenance grants and scrapping undergraduate tuition fees, with long-term plans to cancel graduate debt.

source.quote: We would fully fund every higher education student, restoring maintenance grants and scrapping undergraduate tuition fees. Our long-term plans also include seeking to cancel the injustice of graduate debt.

policies.policy_title: Increase public transport subsidies and investment
policies.stated: Increase annual public subsidies for rail and bus travel to £10bn by the end of the next parliament, and invest an additional £19bn over five years to improve public transport, support electrification, and invest in new cycleways and footpaths, reallocating road building funds.

source.quote: Green MPs will push to: • Increase annual public subsidies for rail and bus travel to £10bn by the end of the next parliament to make public transport reliable, frequent, accessible and affordable, including free bus travel for under-18s. • Invest an additional £19bn over five years to improve public transport, support electrification and invest in new cycleways and footpaths; this includes the reallocation of funding earmarked for road building.

policies.policy_title: Bring railways into public ownership and invest in modernisation
policies.stated: Bring the railways back into public ownership, invest in a modern, efficient, electrified railway with affordable fares, and gradually bring train companies back into public ownership as contracts expire.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for: • Investment in a modern, efficient, publicly owned railway, with affordable fares. • Greater investment in more rapid electrification so the rail network can be powered sustainably. • Bring the railways back into public ownership. • Train companies to be gradually brought back into public ownership, as existing contracts expire and rolling stock which is currently owned by leasing companies needs replacement.

policies.policy_title: Phase out petrol and diesel vehicles and introduce road pricing
policies.stated: Restore the fuel-duty escalator, oppose new road building, end sales of new petrol and diesel vehicles by 2027, end their use on the road by 2035, and introduce a £5bn per year vehicle scrappage scheme, supported by EV charging rollout. Introduce road-pricing.

source.quote: Green MPs will push to restore the fuel-duty escalator to this end and, as revenue declines, we favour the introduction of road-pricing, designed to ensure the protection of users’ privacy. Greens will oppose all new road building plans. Within a decade we want to see all petrol and diesel vehicles replaced by Electric Vehicles (EVs). We would push for an extensive vehicle scrappage scheme to support this rapid transition to EVs, with funding rising to £5bn per year by the end of the parliament, supported by the rapid rollout of EV charging points. Elected Greens would therefore also push for: • An end to sales of new petrol and diesel fuelled vehicles by 2027 and to the use of petrol and diesel vehicles on the road by 2035.

policies.policy_title: Reduce reliance on aviation and halt airport expansion
policies.stated: Introduce a frequent-flyer levy, ban domestic flights for journeys less than three hours by train, apply carbon tax to aviation kerosene, halt airport capacity expansion, and invest in skills for aviation workers to transition to alternative jobs.

source.quote: Green MPs will campaign for: • A frequent-flyer levy to reduce the impact of the 15% of people who take 70% of flights. • A ban on domestic flights for a journey that would take less than three hours by train. • An end to the implicit subsidy for flying that results from kerosene being exempt from fuel duty: the carbon tax would apply to all kerosene for aviation sold in the UK • A halt to any expansion of airport capacity. • Investment in skills so that aviation and airport workers can move into rewarding alternative jobs as the number of flights declines.

policies.policy_title: Introduce a Fair Politics Act and reform democracy
policies.stated: Introduce a Fair Politics Act to repeal the Elections Act 2022, restore Electoral Commission powers, replace first-past-the-post with proportional representation, introduce state funding for political parties, and remove cap on Electoral Commission fines.

source.quote: Elected Greens will introduce a Fair Politics Act to strengthen our democracy now. This legislation would do the following: • Repeal the anti-democratic Elections Act 2022, ending the need to provide voter-ID. • Restore the Electoral Commission’s power to prosecute, and abolish the barriers to third-party campaigning so that all groups can be transparently involved in the democratic process. • Replace the first-past-the-post system for parliamentary and council elections with a fair and proportional voting system. • Introduce a fair system of state funding for political parties to eliminate dependence on large private donations. • Remove the cap on fines that can be imposed by the Electoral Commission on political parties that have been found to have breached electoral law.

policies.policy_title: Replace the House of Lords and lower voting age
policies.stated: Replace the House of Lords with an elected second chamber, give 16 and 17-year-olds the right to vote and stand for election, and introduce residence-based voting rights.

source.quote: Our priorities will be: • Replacing the House of Lords with an elected second chamber. • Votes for 16-year-olds and residence-based voting rights. • Give 16 and 17-year-olds the right to vote and to stand for parliament and other elected offices.

policies.policy_title: Defend human rights and civil liberties
policies.stated: Defend the Human Rights Act, support continued direct access to ECHR rights, restore legal aid for public law cases, protect religious expression, and scrap the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act and Public Order Act.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Defend the Human Rights Act. • Support continued direct access to ECHR rights in the domestic courts. • Restore legal aid for public law cases so everybody can uphold their rights in court. • Protect the right to religious expression. • Scrap the Police, Crime, Sentencing and Courts Act, Public Order Act and other legislation that erodes the right to protest and to free expression.

policies.policy_title: Support self-ID for trans and non-binary people and end spousal veto
policies.stated: Support self-ID for trans and non-binary people to be legally recognised in their chosen gender. End the spousal veto for married trans people to acquire gender recognition certificates and allow an X gender marker on passports.

source.quote: The Green Party supports self-ID, so that trans and non-binary people could be legally recognised in their chosen gender through self-declaration. We also support ending the spousal veto so that married trans people can acquire their gender recognition certification without having to obtain permission from their spouse, and to change the law so an X gender marker can be added to passports for non-binary and intersex people who wish to use it.

policies.policy_title: Increase local government funding and devolved powers
policies.stated: Increase local government funding across England by £5bn per year. Give the Welsh Government the same devolved powers as the Scottish Government in advance of a new constitutional settlement, and support the Senedd if it decides to hold an independence referendum.

source.quote: Elected Greens will ensure that local authorities across England are given the powers and resources they need. They will push for an increase in local government funding of £5bn per year to tackle the current under-funding crisis. Elected Greens would give the Welsh Government the same devolved powers as the Scottish Government in advance of a new constitutional settlement. Elected Greens will support the Senedd if it decides to hold an independence referendum.

policies.policy_title: End the hostile environment and create safe routes to sanctuary
policies.stated: End the hostile environment, abolish the No Recourse to Public Funds condition, and end minimum income requirements for spouses of work visa holders. Establish safe routes for those fleeing persecution, war, or climate disaster, with fast and fair asylum processes and permission to work.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for: • An end to the hostile environment. • An end to the minimum income requirements for spouses of those holding work visas. Green MPs would campaign to abolish the No Recourse to Public Funds condition. Elected Greens will push for: • The United Kingdom to work with other countries to establish safe routes by which those fleeing persecution, war, or climate disaster may arrive in the country of their choice to make their case without having to risk their lives. • A fast and fair process to assess asylum applications. • Those seeking asylum and protection to be permitted to work while their application is being decided.

policies.policy_title: Reform the Home Office and simplify visa applications
policies.stated: Dismantle the Home Office, creating a Department of Migration and a Department of Justice. Simplify visa applications, process them swiftly and empathetically, charge only cost-price application fees, and ensure free and comprehensive NHS access for visa-holding migrants.

source.quote: We will push to dismantle the dysfunctional Home Office and create a new Department of Migration alongside a Department of Justice, thus separating functions around migration and citizenship from the criminal justice system. The system of visa applications should be simplified and all applications should be processed swiftly, and with empathy and intelligence. We would seek the end to the exploitation of people for profit and only charge application fees at cost. Access to the NHS should be free and comprehensive for migrants with visas.

policies.policy_title: Invest in local arts, sport, and culture
policies.stated: Invest an extra £5bn over 5 years for local government spending on arts and culture, including museums, theatres, libraries, and galleries. Protect the night-time economy, permit local authorities to invest in professional sports clubs, and allow access to school sports facilities outside teaching hours.

source.quote: To support local culture and sport, elected Greens will campaign to: • Invest an extra £5bn over 5 years for local government spending on arts and culture to fund keeping local museums, theatres, libraries and art galleries open and thriving. • Protect the night-time economy through a review of planning regulations and giving local authorities the powers to ensure there is space for cultural life. • Permit local authorities to invest in shares in professional sports clubs which operate in their area as a means of maintaining a connection between the club and its community. • Allow access to school sports facilities by local clubs and teams outside teaching hours to ensure maximum use of a valuable resource.

policies.policy_title: Introduce a Digital Bill of Rights and regulate AI
policies.stated: Introduce a Digital Bill of Rights to establish UK standards for rule of law and democracy in digital spaces, ensuring independent regulation of social media, safeguarding elections, and giving the public control over data. Push for a precautionary regulatory approach to AI, aligning with European and global efforts.

source.quote: Elected Greens would push to establish the UK as a leading voice on standards for the rule of law and democracy in digital spaces with a Digital Bill of Rights to ensure independent regulation of social media providers. The Digital Bill of Rights will give the public greater control over their data, ensuring UK data protection is as strong as any other regulatory regime. Elected Greens will push for a precautionary regulatory approach to the harms and risk of AI. We would align the UK approach with our neighbours in Europe, UNESCO and global efforts to support a coordinated response to future risks of AI.

policies.policy_title: Reform media ownership and support local news
policies.stated: Tighten rules on media ownership so no individual or company owns more than 20% of a media market. Implement the 2012 Leveson Report recommendations and reinstate the second part of the review. Support local media with new grants.

source.quote: Elected Greens will push for rules on media to be tightened so that no individual or company owns more than 20% of a media market. We would implement the recommendations of the 2012 Leveson Report and reinstate the second part of that crucial review to ensure the UK media are held to the highest ethical standards. We will support local media through new grants to encourage the growth of a wider range of civic-minded local news publishers.

policies.policy_title: Restore trust in police and end disproportionate policing tactics
policies.stated: Restore trust and confidence in the police by acknowledging institutional racism, misogyny, homophobia, and disablism. End the routine use of stop and search and facial recognition software, and implement ongoing fitness-to-practice assessments on diversity for all officers.

source.quote: We believe in policing by consent, but this can only work if the police can rebuild trust with the communities they serve. Police Services need to acknowledge the institutional racism, misogyny, homophobia and disablism that have dominated policing for so long. Elected Greens will push for: • An end to the routine use of stop and search and to the use of facial recognition software. • Police Services to deliver ongoing fitness to practice assessments on diversity for all police officers and relevant civilian staff.

policies.policy_title: Invest in criminal justice and reduce court backlogs
policies.stated: Invest £11bn in restoring the Ministry of Justice budget to repair court buildings, restore legal aid, and ensure the Criminal Bar is sufficiently funded. Recruit more judges representative of wider society to reduce court backlogs.

source.quote: The Green Party will invest £11bn in restoring the Ministry of Justice budget over the course of the next parliament. This would be used to restore legal aid budgets, to ensure that the Criminal Bar is sufficiently well funded and to repair court buildings. Elected Greens will push to recruit more judges and to ensure that they are representative of wider society.

policies.policy_title: Prioritise restorative justice and rehabilitation over short prison sentences
policies.stated: Expand restorative justice and legislate for a presumption against custodial sentences under two years to reduce reoffending. Implement diversion programmes for low-level drug and alcohol offences and young offenders, focusing on rehabilitation through investment in probation and prison services.

source.quote: Green MPs will expand restorative justice when crimes do take place, both to give victims a voice and to help offenders take responsibility for the harm they have done. Elected Greens will seek to break the cycle of reoffending through legislating for a presumption against custodial sentences under two years. Elected Greens will ensure that diversion programmes are in place for: • All low-level drug and alcohol related offences. • Young offenders arrested for low-level offences.

policies.policy_title: End violence against women and girls (VAWG)
policies.stated: Make misogyny a hate crime across the UK and increase police capacity to deal with domestic violence. Develop a new UK-wide strategy to tackle gender-based violence, ensure it's a measurable police priority, and fully fund local authorities for domestic violence and rape crisis provision. Decriminalise sex work.

source.quote: It is a Green Party priority to end domestic abuse and violence against women and girls. Elected Greens will push to: • Make misogyny a hate crime across the UK and increase the police’s capacity to deal with domestic violence. • Develop and implement a new UK-wide strategy to tackle gender-based violence, including domestic violence, rape and sexual abuse, Female Genital Mutilation (FGM), and trafficking. • Ensure that domestic abuse and gender-based violence is a key measurable priority for all police forces and that all police officers are trained to recognise and tackle domestic violence. • Fund local authorities so that domestic violence, rape crisis and other provision can meet local needs. • Decriminalise sex work.

policies.policy_title: Decriminalise personal drug possession
policies.stated: Push to decriminalise personal possession of drugs, diverting individuals from the criminal justice system to health-focused support for addiction, housing, and employment.

source.quote: Elected Greens will therefore push to decriminalise personal possession of drugs, diverting people from the criminal justice system towards support with addiction, housing and employment, from health workers focused on drug harm reduction.

policies.policy_title: Support Ukraine and advocate for reform of European security architecture
policies.stated: Continue to support Ukraine against Russian invasion and work towards reform of the European security architecture and disarmament, based on democratic and inclusive values, and mutual transparency.

source.quote: The Green Party wants to see the UK: • Continue to support Ukraine as it resists Russian invasion. • Work towards reform of the European security architecture and disarmament, based on shared commitments to democracy and mutual transparency.

policies.policy_title: Advocate for a permanent ceasefire and political solution in Israel and Palestine
policies.stated: Push for an immediate and permanent bilateral ceasefire, return of hostages, a durable political solution ensuring security and equal rights for Israelis and Palestinians, recognition of the state of Palestine, and an end to illegal occupation. Investigate and prosecute war crimes and end UK arms exports to Israel.

source.quote: Green MPs will push for: • An immediate and permanent bilateral ceasefire. • A durable political solution that ensures security and equal rights for Israelis and Palestinians. This is the only way to achieve long-term security for the people of Palestine and Israel. • Recognition of the state of Palestine and an urgent international effort to end the illegal occupation of Palestinian land. • Investigation and prosecution of war crimes. • An end to all UK arms exports to and military cooperation with Israel, which make the British government complicit in these war crimes.

policies.policy_title: Increase overseas aid and climate finance
policies.stated: Restore international aid to 0.7% of GNI, raising it to 1% by 2033. Increase the climate finance budget to 1.5% of GNI by 2033, with an additional contribution to a newly established Loss and Damage Fund. Make finance and technology available to support low-income countries in climate action.

source.quote: Greens would ensure that the UK’s existing climate finance commitments are delivered in full and are genuinely new and additional to aid spending. Elected Greens would push for the UK to: • Go beyond restoring international aid to 0.7% of GNI, raising this to 1% by 2033. • Increase the climate finance budget to 1.5% of GNI by 2033, with an additional contribution to a newly established Loss and Damage Fund in order to help climate vulnerable countries to respond to increasingly severe storms, floods and rising temperatures. • Make finance and technology available to support the development of environmentally and socially sustainable economies of low-income countries to tackle the causes and impacts of the climate and nature emergencies.

policies.policy_title: Rejoin the European Union
policies.stated: Work towards rejoining the EU as soon as politically feasible. Join the Customs Union as a first step, followed by a speedy return to free movement of people and rejoining the Erasmus Programme.

source.quote: Green MPs will work towards: • Re-joining the EU as soon as the domestic political situation is favourable and EU member states are willing. • Joining the Customs Union as a first step towards full EU membership, and a way of resolving many of the worst problems resulting from Brexit. • A speedy return to the free movement of people between the UK and the EU, including reciprocal rights to work for both UK and European citizens. • Rejoining the Erasmus Programme, which enables students to study for a year in another European country.

policies.policy_title: Dismantle nuclear weapons and cancel Trident
policies.stated: Push for the UK to sign the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW), dismantle nuclear weapons, cancel the Trident programme, and remove all foreign nuclear weapons from UK soil.

source.quote: Elected Greens will: • Push for the UK to sign the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons (TPNW), and following this to begin immediately the process of dismantling our nuclear weapons, cancelling the Trident programme and removing all foreign nuclear weapons from UK soil.

excluded.reason: This is a legislative vehicle for specific environmental policies, which are detailed elsewhere.

coverage_note: Policies were primarily extracted from the Green Party's 2024 General Election Manifesto (PDF). No additional material policies meeting the strict criteria for distinct, attributable commitments and plausibly moving a fundamental were found on the Green Party's official website (greenparty.org.uk/about/our-manifesto/) that were not already covered by or implicitly included within the manifesto text.
